newsitem.title: USA: Nintendo says sales of device top 1 mln.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo says sales of device top 1 mln.

text.p: Nintendo Co Ltd said Monday that sales of its new Nintendo 64 video game machine have topped one million units in the first 10 weeks of availability in Japan.
In a statement issued by the company's U.S. subsidiary in Redmond, Wash., the company said more than 90 percent of units shipped had sold through to consumers.
The company said sales of its Super Mario 64 game also have topped one million units.
The new 64-bit game system will be released in the United States Sept. 29, one year behind schedule, and Nintendo officials said they expected demand to exceed supply for the upcoming holiday season.
Initial U.S. shipments are expected to be no more than 600,000 units, compared with retail requests for more than one million units by Christmas, Nintendo said.
"We're asking our parent company to do everything possible to increase total shipments to North America," Peter Main, executive vice president of Nintendo of America, said in a statment.
The cartridge game console will retail for a suggested $199.95. The company said 12 games for the machine will be available by Christmas, with most carrying a suggested retail price of $69.95.
